context: DEC-007 requires namespaced ids; source families collide and several have no stable key (lesson ordinals, fh rows repeating L3/T1, rigor-atlas integer technique ids, crate names repeated across repos).
decision: Adopt the id grammar in contracts/IF-ID.md: per-family derivation from a source-native key, lessons as fr:lesson-<topic>-<repo>, fh rows grouped per layer/technique, ra:technique:<repo>/<entity>/<h8 of technique text>, crate:<repo>/<crate> with ~<h6 of manifest path> only on repeated (repo, crate) pairs, a retirement ledger for any id that disappears, and the 19-line validator regex block as the machine form.
alternatives: ordinal ids per family (renumber on insert)
rigor-atlas techniques.id integers (assigned at build, not stable)
crate:<crate-name> alone (4 names repeat across repos)
automatic counters on collision
rationale: Every key is written in the source or is a hash of the item's own text, so a rebuild from the same bytes yields the same ids; the scratch minting of all 3,474 v1 ids gives 0 duplicates and 0 ids matching zero or two families.
consequences: Retitling a heading or editing a rigor-atlas technique text changes an id and needs a retirement row (gate Q6). GoldenSet ebac079 already uses this grammar.
reversibility: reversible before the first index ships; after that, only through retirement rows
amendment_trigger: a new source family, or a derivation key that proves unstable in practice (gate Q6 firing on unchanged content)

context: S03 needs one entry shape for every result; REQ-O3 requires tier or verdict, license and source link on every result.
decision: Adopt fr.search.entry/v1 (contracts/IF-ENTRY.schema.json, JSON Schema 2020-12) as the logical entry, with a required posture field, a required prompt template id, required credit, and quote optional and stored only in the quotes shard.
alternatives: free-form entries per source
separate schemas per namespace
posture implied from prose
rationale: A closed schema lets gate Q1 reject a missing license or an unpinned link mechanically; posture and template ids make the no-overclaim rule checkable without parsing prose.
consequences: Every generator field is fixed now; S05 may pack entries but must unpack to this schema; facets stay open until S05 contracts ranking.
evidence: IF-ENTRY.md §5: 3 real examples valid, 17 planted mutations rejected (jsonschema 4.25.1)
amendment_trigger: S05 needs a field the schema forbids, or a golden-set review shows a card missing information readers need

context: REQ-O4 wants the index rebuilt on every deploy, but the crate directory needs network reads and the fh and rigor-atlas catalogs cannot be rebuilt in Actions (charter Constraints, UNK-010).
decision: Two-stage build: network collectors (crates in Actions; fh and rigor-atlas by hand under a written procedure) commit dated, hashed snapshots listed in search/snapshots/SNAPSHOTS.tsv; an offline, deterministic generator reads only committed files and commits the shards; gate Q2 reruns it and diffs byte for byte (the K4 pattern).
alternatives: generate in deploy only, uncommitted (breaks gate S stamps and file:// Gate I on the committed tree)
read fh/rigor-atlas from private paths at build (forbidden by the charter)
call GitHub from the generator (nondeterministic)
rationale: Matches the existing make-stack.mjs discipline and the watch workflow that already commits and redeploys; keeps every deploy reproducible from the repo alone.
consequences: The daily watch must run the crate collector; the crate snapshot has an 8-day age limit; fh and rigor-atlas refreshes stay manual (UNK-009).
amendment_trigger: the crate collector cannot stay within GitHub API limits, or a snapshot source gains a public rebuild path

context: Links to this repo's own files must be pinned, but a committed deterministic index cannot know the commit it will be committed in.
decision: Pin this repo's own copy targets and source_url at the release tag v<package.json version> (the make-stack.mjs rule) and make the on-site url, which deploys with the index, the primary link for fr: entries; pin every other repository at a 40-hex commit.
alternatives: pin at HEAD (fixed-point problem)
pin at the last commit touching each source file (fails when source and index land in one commit)
link branches (drift, forbidden by HON-03)
rationale: Reuses the existing convention; the site link is always current, so tag drift between releases (intake-IntakeFR2 U13) affects only the secondary GitHub link.
consequences: GitHub line links for fr: sources edited after the last tag may point one or more lines off until the next release.
amendment_trigger: readers report wrong-line links, or releases become rare enough that drift is routine

context: Shards must load from file:// (Gate I) and bust the fr.zeststream.ai zone cache that ignores max-age=0 on /assets/*.
decision: Three script-global shards (search-core.js stamped by shell.mjs; search-deep.js and search-quotes.js loaded at runtime by ?v= taken from core), one build id shared by all three and computed as in IF-SHARD.md §3, and client skew handling that never mixes builds.
alternatives: JSON files fetched at runtime (fetch from file:// fails, per intake inference)
content-hashed filenames (the site stamps with ?v= today)
one monolithic index (breaks the core budget)
rationale: Same mechanism as data.js and shell.mjs stamps; the static host ignores ?v=, so the build id is the only reliable skew signal.
consequences: Gate Q7 must check runtime-loaded versions that gate S cannot see; the file:// loading of the deep shard is an inference until gate Q5 proves it.
amendment_trigger: SearchPerfProbe shows lazy script loading misses the REQ-O2 budgets, or a CSP is introduced that forbids injected scripts

context: DEC-009 allows short quotes, but UNK-008 (crawler policy, HUMAN_DECISION) is open and DEC-008 is only proposed.
decision: Ship the quotes shard empty while search/crawler-policy is pending; gate Q3 (HON-15) enforces it. When the maintainer decides UNK-008, the policy file changes and quotes flow.
alternatives: ship quotes now with no crawler rule
ship quotes now with DEC-008 robots rules applied before the decision
rationale: Publishing rider-covered text under an undecided crawler policy cannot be undone once crawled; an empty shard costs nothing and every other feature ships.
consequences: Cards show links and license but no quotes until the decision; the crate description quote in IF-ENTRY.examples.json stays an example.

context: UNK-007 (BLOCKS_BUILD for the rigor-atlas and fh ingest beads) asks how KNOW/INFER/GUESS and fh citation states map onto RULEBOOK §1 tiers.
decision: Adopt contracts/TIER-MAP.md: rules TM-RA-1..9 and TM-FH-1..8, weaker tier on any ambiguity, tier by cited evidence path (docs-only KNOW is a maintainer claim), no High confidence for any agent-produced label, unmapped labels fail the build, mapped_from recorded on every entry.
alternatives: intake-IntakeRigor2 §8 suggestion (KNOW→Tier 1, INFER→Inference, GUESS→Maintainer claim) without the evidence-path split
show atlas labels verbatim beside Rulebook tiers (two vocabularies on one card)
exclude all atlas/fh items
rationale: Measured on the DB: 34 KNOW techniques cite only docs and 3 GUESS techniques cite code, so a label-only map would overstate 34 rows; RULEBOOK.md:53 makes a second agent a cross-check, not independence.
consequences: 1,412 techniques Tier 1 Medium, 34 + 11 Tier 3, 19 + 3 Tier 5, all profiles and prescriptions Tier 5; 52 fh exemplars Tier 1 Medium; lossiness listed in TIER-MAP.md §5.
evidence: TIER-MAP.md §4 (fh_quote_check.py: 52/52 CURRENT on the local mirror)
amendment_trigger: the independent reviewer rejects a rule, or a re-grade of a KNOW sample shows the atlas reading wrong often enough to demote TM-RA-1
revised: 2026-09-25 after review 5 (Luna, SIGN-WITH-CORRECTIONS): TM-RA-1 now requires a build-time evidence check (new TM-RA-10 for the rest); principle 4 names the tm_unmapped_label detector and its failure codes; principle 6 makes every Tier-1 basis a template that separates what was checked (the cited text is at the pinned lines) from the unchecked interpretation; TIER-MAP §4.1 normalizes the raw checker states (RELOCATED, NO_REVISION, empty quote) before any rule reads them. Fixtures: contracts/fixtures/tier-map.json; every rule is in contracts/gate-matrix.tsv.

context: REQ-O3 requires every result to show its evidence tier or verdict, but 104 of 136 rigor practices, the checklist, lessons, runbook steps and rigor-atlas kinds carry no tier of their own (intake-IntakeFR2 U5, HUMAN_DECISION).
decision: Add the evidence scheme "ungraded": tier, label and confidence null, a basis sentence saying the item is cited but not tiered, shown as a visible badge. Items take a tier only from a tag on their own cited source.
alternatives: grade the 104 practices now (a new judgment outside the cohort lane)
inherit a tier from the repos in evidenced_in (upgrades without evidence)
hide ungraded items
rationale: Saying "ungraded" is honest and satisfies "shows its evidence tier or verdict" with an explicit value; inventing tiers would be proof-class inflation.
consequences: Many practice cards will read "Ungraded"; the maintainer may prefer grading them in a later bead.
amendment_trigger: the maintainer decides these items must carry a tier (HUMAN_DECISION on intake U5)

context: REQ-O3 bars telling a reader to use a repository whose verdict says not to, but postures live in packet prose and no structured field exists.
decision: Create search/verdict-posture.tsv (repo, posture, path, lines) re-encoding each existing verdict with a K2-style citation; ring gives the default (Invest→use, Pilot→pilot, Explore→watch, Monitor→reference-only), an explicit packet sentence overrides it; crates, capabilities and profiles inherit their repository's posture; repositories without a verdict are unassessed.
alternatives: derive posture from the ring alone
parse packet prose at build time
no posture (imperatives everywhere)
rationale: A cited table keeps the judgment where it was made (the packet) and makes HON-04/HON-05 checkable.
consequences: A bead fills 44 + 21 rows; 13 packets contain a matching phrase today (a phrase count, not yet a posture table; IF-SOURCES.md §6); Explore (34 repos) becomes watch, so their crates get evaluate-only prompts.
amendment_trigger: a reviewer finds a posture row that reads as a new verdict rather than a restatement

context: UNK-005 (ASSUME_REVERSIBLY: one template per kind) needs a concrete template set before S06 can build prompts.
decision: Resolve UNK-005 with one base template per kind and posture variants for the software kinds: 24 versioned templates for 17 kinds (IF-PROMPT.md §2), each ending in a proof request, with fixed license sentences per class.
alternatives: one generic template
hand-written prompt per entry
model-written prompts at build time
rationale: Kinds need different proofs (planted known-bad, benchmark, falsification experiment, back-out plan); posture in the template id makes the no-overclaim rule mechanical.
consequences: S09 golden-set review rates prompts; the falsifier in IF-PROMPT.md §4 triggers a rewrite.
reversibility: reversible (templates regenerate every prompt in one build)
amendment_trigger: a template is rated generic or wrong at least twice or in 20% of its golden-set samples

context: Crate descriptions are Jeffrey's text (rider-covered manifests) but are the main matching text for REQ-U3 queries; quotes must never be in the core shard.
decision: Class A crate summaries (211) are our own one-line paraphrases written and reviewed in a bead; manifest descriptions ship only as quotes in the quotes shard; keywords (single terms) may be facets.
alternatives: treat descriptions as metadata and ship them in core
templated fact-only summaries for every crate
rationale: Keeps core free of verbatim upstream text (HON-12) without losing matching for the crates people search for most.
consequences: A 211-summary authoring bead with review; deep-shard crates get fact-only summaries plus keywords.
amendment_trigger: the maintainer rules descriptions are metadata, not quotes

context: DEC-003 names the v1 sources but not every exclusion the intakes found.
decision: Exclude from v1: forks (bun, exacl, ffn, gonode, hnswlib-rs, rust-block, textract-py3, wezterm), fh oracles D14 and Z1-Z4, the fh doctrine ledger, the capability replaces column, rigor-atlas hypotheses, entities, essays, lexical hits and notes/author columns, nameless manifests; vendored snapshots keep quote hashes, not quote text.
alternatives: label forks instead of excluding
vendor quote text in snapshots
rationale: Forks are not Jeffrey's work; the excluded fh rows are private; hashes let Actions verify quotes without committing rider text before UNK-008.
consequences: ra techniques 1,479 (18 fork rows out), profiles 137, fh 56 entries, crates 1,289.
